item.title: Postdoctoral Research Associate
item.description: The Princeton Institute for International and Regional Studies (PIIRS) at Princeton University is pleased to announce the call for applications to the PIIRS Postdoctoral Fellowship Program for the 2027-28 academic year. As a leading global institution in interdisciplinary research on international issues, PIIRS is dedicated to advancing innovative scholarship that addresses the world's most pressing challenges. The PIIRS Postdoctoral Fellows Program is integral to that mission. We will award up to four postdoctoral fellowships to our 2027-28 cohort. PIIRS seeks recent PhDs in the Social Sciences who have demonstrated exceptional scholarship, congruent with the Institute's intellectual focus, that simultaneously advances theoretical debates in their disciplinary field; creatively speaks to and engages with a multidisciplinary audience; and deepens substantive regional knowledge of specific places. Appointments will be made at the rank of Postdoctoral Research Associate and are for one year (12 months) with the possibility of renewal pending satisfactory performance and continued funding. Postdoctoral Research Associates are expected to be in residence at Princeton or the local vicinity for the entire academic year or demonstrate to the program’s satisfaction the ability to be on campus on a daily basis and on short notice in order to fulfill responsibilities relating to in-person participation. The position requires Postdoctoral Research Associates to be on campus at least four days per week. Leveraging Princeton's scholarly resources, fellows will focus on research, expand their intellectual horizons, and prepare work for publication. They will have biweekly meetings with the faculty director to share their work, and monthly meetings with faculty fellows from various social sciences to present their work and learn from others. Fellows are also encouraged to engage with colleagues and attend departmental seminars. Applicants must demonstrate outstanding scholarly achievement and promise. To be eligible, applicants generally cannot have more than two years of postdoctoral experience prior to the start of the appointment, at the beginning of the academic year on September 1, 2027. The postdoctoral selection will be made based on the strength of the candidates' scholarly record; the promise of the proposed research; and the ability to contribute to the intellectual life of the postdoctoral program (with interest in connecting with other PIIRS and Princeton departments on campus). In addition to a competitive salary and benefits, the program will provide the Fellow with the opportunity to host a small, pre-publication, book workshop; and a research fund of $4,000 per year. The program will also provide shared office space, and a laptop computer. Further information can be found at here . This position is subject to the University's background check policy. The work location for this position is in-person on campus at Princeton University. Position is not eligible for sponsorship of an H-1B visa requiring consular processing; other visa sponsorships (including H-1B visas not requiring consular processing) may be available, as appropriate. Application Instructions Applications are due by September 15, 2026 (11:59 p.m. EST). The following application items should be uploaded by the applicant: Cover letter Curriculum vitae Transcripts Research Proposal indicating plans for two-year postdoc (maximum 5 pages double-spaced) Dissertation abstract (including Table of Contents) Writing sample: one chapter of the dissertation or one published article related to dissertation topic. Document confirming either that you have completed all requirements for the PhD degree or a letter signed by your dissertation advisor indicating that you will complete the PhD by the start date of the fellowship. The names and email addresses of three referees, who will be contacted automatically by the online application system with an invitation to upload their letter of recommendation to the system by the application deadline. (**Please note: all letters of reference should be submitted by your referees before September 15, 2026. deadline. **) Equal Employment Opportunity Statement Princeton University is an Equal Opportunity Employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

item.description: The Account Manager delivers public affairs, stakeholder engagement and communications consultancy across infrastructure projects. The role spans client and internal work, and involves close collaboration with the wider team and freelancers. The AM is a strong collaborator with an entrepreneurial spirit — proactive, willing to ask questions and raise ideas, with the tenacity to go beyond the brief. Drawing on consultancy and/or in-house experience, they identify compelling narratives and opportunities, and drive advocacy with political, business and other stakeholders. Duties & Responsibilities The Account Manager will: Demonstrate IM values and behaviours in all ways of working. Deliver impactful campaigns and high-quality materials to support client objectives. Manage relationships with senior project stakeholders and clients, and with a wide range of external stakeholders — business leaders, local and national government, special interest groups and local communities. Develop stakeholder mapping, manage stakeholder databases, produce briefing notes and identify potential advocates. Work with technical experts across client teams to translate complex information for varied audiences. Progress to leading client accounts and project-managing deliverables, team members, and hours/billing. Work with graphic designers and videographers on infographics, animations, video case studies, presentations, brochures and maps. Support the IM leadership team on corporate materials and projects. Assist in developing new business pitches and proposals. Monitor Government and Parliament activity relevant to clients and business development. Research new infrastructure projects and developments in planning policy. Take on other duties as needed to maintain a high standard of work. Person Specification Demonstrable interest in and knowledge of UK politics, including local, regional and devolved government, policy and infrastructure. High level of collaboration. Skilled communicator, written and spoken. Track record of building and managing relationships. Campaigning mindset. Enthusiastic and entrepreneurial. Comfortable with stakeholders at all levels, from junior staff to CEOs. Experience in a relevant field, with the ability to translate this into positive outcomes for the team. item.description: The Home Office works to build a safe, fair and prosperous UK. We achieve this through our work on counter-terrorism, policing, crime, drugs policy, immigration and passports. The Corporate Services Group works closely with the Home Office’s policy and operational commands to enable us together to deliver the department’s priorities. The group is comprised of different teams and professional functions, including Commercial, Communications, Finance, People, Portfolio and Project Delivery, Private Office, Security, Estates and Information. As a member of the Communications Directorate, you’ll be supporting our mission to deliver outstanding public services that work for everyone. You will join a multi-disciplinary team with colleagues based across the UK, working together to deliver the Home Office’s communications strategy. We believe a positive, open and supportive culture is crucial to help everyone deliver their best work. We value diversity and provide an inclusive and encouraging environment for our team members. We nurture our talent and offer a broad range of learning and development opportunities to help you fulfil your potential. Successful applicants will be a highly motivated, adaptable, innovative, dependable and collaborative communications professional, prepared to work on some of the most challenging, high profile and interesting issues in government. You will support the planning, delivery and evaluation of communications campaigns aligned to major government priorities, such as securing the border, reducing illegal migration and tackling knife crime, to create measurable change among audiences. You will work with a multi-disciplinary team, including press, marketing, insight, internal communications, external affairs and social media specialists. And you will build and maintain positive relationships with internal and external stakeholders. You will be expected to manage content production and work with agencies where needed, while also having the opportunity to bring your own creative ideas to life. This will involve managing plans, ensuring activity remains on schedule and delivering value for money. item.description: The Royal British Legion is looking for a confident and politically aware Public Affairs and Campaigns Officer to lead impactful campaigning activity across the North of England, including North East, North West, and Yorkshire & the Humber regions of England. This is an opportunity to work at the heart of issues affecting the Armed Forces community, turning insight into action and ensuring the voices of veterans, serving personnel and their families are heard where it matters most. From influencing local decision-makers to shaping meaningful conversations across communities, you’ll play a visible role in driving positive change on behalf of those who have served. We’re looking for someone who understands how local government and public affairs really work; someone who can build credibility quickly, spot opportunities to influence and create campaigns that connect with people on a local level. You’ll be equally comfortable briefing MPs and councillors, working alongside community stakeholders, organising events and translating national priorities into campaigns that feel relevant and tangible within local communities. This role would suit someone who thrives on relationship-building, enjoys working across a varied political landscape and has the confidence to represent a nationally respected organisation in high-profile settings. In return, you’ll join a passionate and collaborative team working on issues that genuinely matter. No two days will look the same, and the impact of your work will be visible across the region. Whether you’re developing local campaign networks, supporting Armed Forces Covenant activity or helping influence policy conversations at a grassroots level, you’ll have the freedom to bring fresh thinking, new ideas and your own approach to engagement. If you’re motivated by purpose, skilled at influencing others and want to be part of an organisation committed to making a lasting difference to the Armed Forces community, we’d love to hear from you. item.title: Member Governance Officer
item.description: We are looking for a highly organised, professional, and impartial Member Governance Officer to join our Member Governance Team based in our Leeds office. The Member Governance team is a small but effective team that sits within the wider Member Services Team and plays a crucial role in ensuring the resolution of disciplinary matters relating to Party members. Member Governance Officers are responsible for conducting investigations in accordance with the Party’s Code of Conduct and associated Rules. They make the initial assessments on if a complaint falls under the Code and then manage the progression of the case under the Party’s processes. The role includes the handling and processing of sensitive and sometimes protracted disciplinary matters which must be handled impartially, empathetically, and professionally. Member Governance Officers must offer support to other colleagues in the handling of disciplinary matters and complaints as well supporting with the work of the Disciplinary Sub-Committee of the Party Board as secretary to hearings. They are responsible for the bulk of the correspondence from the Member Governance Team with them handling dismissals and investigations as well as general correspondence through the complaints management system. They also provide support to the wider Member Services Team in the handling of day-to-day matters in busy periods or when covering annual leave. They work as the primary support to the Designated Safeguarding Lead on safeguarding matters and administration. item.title: Jewish Health Equity Partnership – Programme Director, Project Lead
item.description: Job 1- Programme Director Full time - 5 years Funding Period Salary £48,000-£50,000 Purpose of the role To lead delivery of the Jewish Health Equity Partnership, delivering systems partnerships within the Jewish community, influencing policy and practice across the health sector, and ensuring successful delivery of the programme’s workstreams in collaboration with partners. The Programme Director will lead JHEP’s operational relationships with partners across the Jewish community and the health sector, building relationships to bring about structural change. The postholder will bring experience of project delivery and stakeholder management within the health sector. This would ideally include familiarity with NHS, ICS, health trusts, public health, commissioning, workforce and/or health equity settings, together with a strong understanding of how antisemitism and structural discrimination affect Jewish communities and wider health outcomes. Job 2- Project Lead Part time / 5 year funding period. Salary £30,000 pa (£75,000 FTE) To provide senior strategic leadership and oversight for the programme, ensuring strong governance, high-quality delivery and effective alignment between strategy, partnerships, evidence and impact. The Project Lead will act as a senior ambassador for the programme, supporting external credibility, funder confidence and long-term sustainability. This role sits at the intersection of health inequalities, structural racism, antisemitism and systems change. The postholder will bring senior-level experience of the health sector, ideally including NHS, Integrated Care Systems, public health, commissioning, workforce or health equity settings, together with a strong understanding of how antisemitism and structural discrimination affect Jewish communities and wider health outcomes. This is an opportunity to establish and lead a pioneering national programme that will shape how Jewish health inequalities are understood and addressed across England. About this role As Partnership Director you'll lead our client portfolio and set the direction of our award-winning community crowdfunding partnerships. We've deliberately rebuilt this role around an AI-powered operations hub, so programme tracking and reporting run on automated workflows and the team spends its energy on what actually moves partnerships forward. We particularly welcome applications from Black, Asian and Minority Ethnic people, people with disabilities, and people from lower income and diverse educational backgrounds who may be under-represented in our organisation. item.title: Research and Policy Officer
item.description: Reports to: Research Manager Location: London / Hybrid (two days a week in office – EC1V 0JR) Hours: Full time (35 hours a week) Contract: 2-year fixed term contract (extension subject to funding) Salary: £37,213 NJC SCP 22 (band 22–27 inc. London Weighting) Annual leave: 25 days increasing by one day per year up to a maximum of 30 days (+ 2 additional days + birthday leave + office closure between Christmas and New Year, in addition to public bank holidays). Other benefits: 7% employer pension contribution, cycle to work scheme, annual wellbeing budget and employee wellbeing assistance programme. Introduction The Prison Reform Trust (PRT) was founded in 1981 to inform and influence public debate on prison conditions and the treatment of prisoners, amidst concerns about a projected prison population of 48,000 by 1984. With the prison population in England and Wales projected to rise to as high as 114,800 by March 2028, the charity remains as important to civic society today as it was then. Our mission is clear: we are working to create a just, humane and effective prison system by influencing decision makers, opinion formers and the public to 1) reduce the use of prison; 2) improve treatment and conditions for prisoners; and 3) promote equality and human rights in the justice system. Job purpose The Research and Policy Officer is a new blended role that reflects the close relationship between PRT’s research and policy functions. The successful candidate will play a crucial role in supporting both activities by helping to deliver research projects that drive policy and legislative change, as well as contributing directly to policy activities through evidence reviews and consultation submissions (functionally line managed by the policy and communications manager). The role will also involve assisting with delivery of the PRT’s flagship publication the Bromley Briefings Prison Factfile. You will have a solid foundation in quantitative and qualitative research methods and some experience of using them in applied research, together with an excellent understanding of the penal system in the UK and the associated research literature. If this sounds like you, you will be joining a reputable organisation with exceptional leadership, extensive networks and a proven track record of promoting evidence-based policy to achieve reform. Key responsibilities Research Collect, process and manage quantitative and qualitative data from primary research projects. This will periodically involve countrywide travel for prison visits, sometimes overnight. Carry out quantitative and qualitative analysis in accordance with agreed research designs and analytical frameworks. Support the compilation, management, cleaning and analysis of complex datasets from official sources. Assist with the transcription, coding and synthesis of qualitative material. Undertake literature reviews and rapid evidence syntheses drawing on academic, policy and practitioner sources. Follow established research workflows and quality-assurance processes to ensure outputs are accurate and reliable, including the Bromley Briefings Prison Factfile. Support the maintenance of research databases, documentation and project records. Assist with the production of research reports, briefings and presentations. Contribute to the communication and dissemination of research findings to policymakers, practitioners and the public. Support wider research function tasks, including coordinating meetings, stakeholder engagement and general administration. Policy Contribute to consultation responses, parliamentary briefings and other policy-related outputs. Conduct desk research and literature reviews to inform policy work Assist the Policy and Communications Manager in delivering policy activities. General responsibilities Participate in team meetings and contribute to organisational planning. Represent PRT externally where appropriate. Undertake administrative tasks necessary for the effective functioning of the Policy, Communications and Research team. Carry out any other duties commensurate with the responsibilities of the post. How to apply Please send your CV, cover letter (2 sides A4 maximum) addressing how you meet the above criteria and completed recruitment monitoring form via the 'Apply' button above (e alex.guthrie@prisonreformtrust.org.uk) by 5pm on Monday 24 th August. We must receive all 3 documents to process your application, and we will request any documents not received. Your recruitment monitoring form will be processed separately from your application. If you would like an informal chat about the role please contact our research manager Sophie Ellis, sophie@prisonreformtrust.org.uk . Interviews will be on Monday 21 st September at our offices at 15 Northburgh Street, London EC1V 0JR . Thank you for your interest in working for the Prison Reform Trust. For more information and to download the monitoring form please visit our website: www.prisonreformtrust.org.uk/opportunities

item.description: Claire Hazelgrove MP is looking for a committed and organised Senior Caseworker to join her constituency office. The Senior Caseworker will support Claire to be an active, impactful and approachable MP. You will lead the casework function and work with a Caseworker to provide advice and support to local people on a range of issues. Managing a large caseload, organising MP advice surgeries, and supporting relevant events, you will help resolve problems for local people through communication with government agencies, local authorities, the voluntary sector and other organisations. Holding a senior role in the team, and working with others, you will collate and surface trends which can inform wider policy change efforts of the MP and team. Key Responsibilities: Lead and oversee the casework and wider direct resident support function of the team Deal with large numbers of standard queries, as well as leading on the more complex individual cases - by phone, email, or face to face - in a professional, confidential, caring and sensitive manner Ensure that each case is dealt with promptly, sensitively, confidentially and accurately in accordance with the MP Plan and organise MP advice surgeries, including identifying and booking residents in for appointments, arranging appropriate venues across the constituency Identify and surface trends and produce relevant reports on issues faced by residents, working across the team to support policy change and campaigning efforts led by others in the team on these, and reporting back to residents Support the Caseworker in their continued growth and development Work collaboratively across the team on relevant project work to help residents more easily access support and to highlight the impact of casework in supporting residents Required skills and values: Ability to deal with and prioritise a large and varied caseload, and work well under pressure Ability to manage expectations in sometimes challenging circumstances Excellent interpersonal and written communication skills Ability to work independently as well as effectively as part of a small team Ability and willingness to work outside of normal hours and travel for work occasionally Discretion and professionalism Sympathetic to the aims, values and objectives of the Labour Party Desirable skills Previous casework experience Upon appointment you will be required to comply with the Baseline Personnel Security Standard, undertaken by the Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO). See Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO) page for further info. MPs generally pay staff in accordance with IPSA guidelines . Closing Date : 23 August 2026 Interview/Start Dates Closing time: 10pm Interviews: Thursday 10th September 2026 Start date: To be agreed, and based on notice period, but as soon as possible Application Details Please send a relevant CV and one page covering letter outlining how you meet the job specification and your interest in the role to: clairehazelgrovemp@gmail.com quoting ‘Senior Caseworker Application - Your First and Last Name’ in the subject line. Due to the high volume of expected applications we are only able to contact you if you have been shortlisted. Thank you. Website : http://clairehazelgrove.co.uk

item.title: Caseworker
item.description: This is an opportunity to help make a real difference to people's lives in Chelsea and Fulham. The caseworker will work alongside the established casework and policy teams and be expected to work collaboratively as well as independently. They’ll split the time dealing with both casework and policy enquiries from constituents. Experience in a similar role providing support to individuals will be considered. The position requires excellent communication skills; the ability to speak, write and listen well as well as strong administrative and organisational skills to manage a busy workload. Key Responsibilities Act as a first point of contact for constituents via telephone and email including handling high volumes of enquiries, engaging with a wide range of constituents over the phone, including those who may be distressed or dissatisfied, demonstrating patience, resilience, and professionalism. Supporting the MP in his work with constituents by providing support through liaison with government agencies, local authorities, the voluntary sector and others. Draft responses to constituents on casework and policy matters. Managing, progressing, and monitoring a heavy caseload. Maintaining an up-to-date knowledge of relevant guidelines/legislation. Ensuring cases are dealt with in a sensitive and confidential manner. Working effectively as part of a small team, showing initiative and taking ownership of your work. Person & Job specification Experience of carrying out casework preferred. Strong interpersonal and communication skills. Experience of dealing with challenging individuals in a calm, professional and respectful manner. A high standard of written English with attention to detail. Can prioritise work effectively and work independently. Has excellent administrative and organisational skills. Experience of dealing with sensitive and confidential information. Competent use of IT packages. A commitment to helping people and getting the best results possible for residents. A positive, approachable manner with the ability to contribute to a supportive and good-humoured team environment. Sympathetic to the aims and values of the Labour Party. Occasional evening work might be required. Upon appointment you will be required to comply with the Baseline Personnel Security Standard, undertaken by the Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO). See Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO) page for further info. MPs generally pay staff in accordance with IPSA guidelines . Closing Date : 23 August 2026 Interview/Start Dates We aim to shortlist week beginning 24th August, and interviews will take place the following week. Please indicate your availability to start in your application. If invited to interview you will be required to complete a written exercise. Start Date – ASAP upon appointment. Application Details To apply, please send us a covering letter and CV with the subject line “ Caseworker Vacancy ” to ben.coleman.mp@parliament.uk . In your cover letter, please set out what you think the main issues in Chelsea and Fulham are likely to be in the next few years. Website : http://www.bencoleman.uk

item.title: Communications Officer
item.description: Wendy Chamberlain MP is looking for a highly motivated, professional individual to join her team as a Communications Officer. The role involves producing quality written content, whilst promoting parliamentary and constituency activities, and providing a range of communications support in a fast-paced Westminster environment. Wendy looks forward to hearing from you, if you thrive on making a difference, welcome the challenge of working in a busy political office and want to play an essential part in communicating her work. Key responsibilities • Prepare press releases, liaise with the media, meeting deadlines as appropriate. • Manage and monitor social media ensuring all enquiries are dealt with in a timely manner and escalating where required. • Maintaining and updating the MP’s E-newsletter and website. • Develop engaging and targeted content across a range of platforms. • Monitor media coverage and identify opportunities to promote the MPs work. • Build and maintain strong relationships with local, regional and national media outlets. • Ensure records are kept and information managed confidentially in line with data protection legislation. • Support the MP in her Westminster role when required. • Support the MP’s priorities and communicate effectively with constituents of all demographics to reflect how her work supports concerns in North East Fife. Key Skills • Excellent written and verbal communication with the ability to engage confidently with a range of audiences and deliver key messages. • Excellent organisational skills and strong attention to detail. • The ability to work independently, and as part of a small team. • Manage competing tasks and respond quickly to the changing political environment. • Be able to engage effectively with a range of stakeholders both in Westminster and the Constituency. An understanding of UK parliamentary procedures, government policy, and current affairs is welcomed with an awareness of devolved issues which the MP may reference on behalf of constituents. Travel to the Constituency may be required and occasional work out with business hours. Upon appointment you will be required to comply with the Baseline Personnel Security Standard, undertaken by the Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO). See Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO) page for further info. MPs generally pay staff in accordance with IPSA guidelines . Closing Date : 24 August 2026 Interview/Start Dates Candidates will be contacted week commencing 31st August 2026 with an update and Interviews will be held early September 2026. The first Interview may be held virtually, and the second interview in person. The start date is as soon as possible. Ideally October 2026. Application Details Applicants should send a covering letter (no more than one page) and a CV (maximum two pages) to Arlene.Campbell@parliament.uk When submitting your content, please use the Header “Name – Communications Officer”. If you have any questions in advance of your submission, please email Arlene Campbell. Website : https://www.wendychamberlain.scot/

item.title: Assistant Professor of International Relations (Tenure-Track)
item.description: The Department of Political Science at Northwestern University seeks applications for a full-time, tenure-track Assistant Professor in International Relations to begin on September 1, 2027. We seek candidates who will advance international relations scholarship and engage with important issues in contemporary world politics. The successful applicant will teach a combination of graduate and undergraduate courses. A Ph.D. in Political Science or a closely related field, with International Relations training, is required. ABD applicants who anticipate completion of the doctorate by Fall 2027 will be considered. Applicants must provide a curriculum vitae, cover letter, writing sample, research statement, teaching statement, and three letters of recommendation. Review of applications will begin immediately, and all applications received by September 15 will be given full consideration. To apply, click the 'Apply' button For inquiries about job advertisements or the application process, please contact Stephen Monteiro, Business Administrator in the Political Science Department. stephen.monteiro@northwestern.edu . Salary The expected base pay range for this position is $100,000 - $125,000. This base pay range is for a nine-month academic appointment, does not include summer salary, and is subject to negotiation. Northwestern University has provided a pay range representing its good faith estimate of what the university reasonably expects to pay for the position. The pay offered to the selected candidate will be determined based on factors including (but not limited to) the experience and qualifications of the selected candidate including years since terminal degree, training, and field or discipline; departmental budget availability; internal equity; and external market pay for comparable jobs. Benefits At Northwestern, we are proud to provide meaningful and competitive benefits. The available benefits package for this position will include health, dental, vision, disability, and life insurance; paid medical/sick and parental leave; tuition benefits for the employee and dependents; pre-tax and flex spending accounts for commuting and dependent care; generous retirement savings options; and wellness programs. For a comprehensive overview of available benefits, including eligibility details, visit us at Northwestern Benefits to learn more. Northwestern University is an Equal Opportunity Employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected characteristics, including disability and veteran status. View Northwestern’s non-discrimination statement . Job applicants who wish to request an accommodation in the application or hiring process should contact the Office of Civil Rights and Title IX Compliance. View additional information on the accommodations process .

item.title: Research Assistant/Associate - Postdoctoral Researcher in Modern Dravidian Studies (Fixed Term)
item.description: The Faculty of History wishes to recruit a Research Assistant/Research Associate within the broad field of 'Modern Dravidian History and Politics 1945-to the present, working under the supervision of Professor Shruti Kapila, Professor of History and Politics. The position is endowed by a recent bequest to the School of Humanities and Social Sciences. This is a full-time post for three years, commencing 1 October 2026 or as soon as possible thereafter. The pathways and aims of this research are to build historical and analytical perspectives on welfare in relation to shifts in democracy and statecraft including emerging digital public infrastructure. A combination of methods - archival, data sets and interview based will be essential. The interaction of ideas and institutions with public perception, political languages and democratic outcome will be key. The ideal candidate will be educated to PhD level, with established expertise in South Asian/Tamil history or politics (or clear evidence that completion of such a doctorate is imminent) and will have fluency with the use of research materials in English and Tamil; proven ability to conduct and deliver a high quality research project; be an experienced Microsoft office user, prepared to learn other software tools if required and have the ability and willingness to engage in digital humanities research and public -facing work, in a collaborative and inter-disciplinary capacity. The postholder will undertake innovative research with data sets, archives and interviews on welfare, democracy and postcolonial statecraft and other repositories utilising Tamil language. With the supervision of Professor Shruti Kapila, they will: Write research articles where appropriate from their own work and move towards publishing a monograph at the completion of their postdoctoral fellowship. Work with Prof Kapila on to identify key sources for digital humanities research and to design and manage the public platform for the project as required. Work closely and collaboratively with colleagues including doctoral students and postdoctoral fellows; and further afield, academics, public intellectuals and others. Fully participate in workshops and conferences connected to the project by presenting papers and assisting with arrangements; attend other conferences, held by other associations and groups, when possible. Work with and inter-disciplinary research and writing with a view to presenting ideas and policy perspectives to stakeholders, public and scholarly audiences. Engage with tasks connected to the dissemination activities of the project. More information about the Faculty is available here: https://www.hist.cam.ac.uk/ Fixed-term: The funds for this post are available until 30 September 2029 in the first instance. To apply online for this vacancy and to view further information about the role, please click the 'Apply' button above. Informal enquiries are welcomed and should be directed to: Professor Shruti Kapila ( sk555@cam.ac.uk ) If you have any queries regarding the application process, please contact: hr@hist.cam.ac.uk Please quote reference JJ50616 on your application and in any correspondence about this vacancy. The University actively supports equality, diversity and inclusion and encourages applications from all sections of society. The University has a responsibility to ensure that all employees are eligible to live and work in the UK.

item.title: Digital Communications Officer
item.description: Family Rights Group’s mission is to create a more socially just society in which the child welfare and family justice systems support children to live safely and thrive within their family, while strengthening the family and community networks of those children who cannot live at home. Founded in 1974, our work combines commitment to human rights and social justice with expertise in child welfare law, policy and practice. As Family Rights Group’s Digital Communications Officer, you will work to plan, develop and deliver a range of informed, creative, impactful and accessible digital content for our external audiences to increase visibility and engagement with the charity’s work and to meet our strategic objectives. You will be responsible for the ideation, production, editing, and publishing of standout content that reaches diverse audiences, including policy-makers and politicians, donors and supporters, and families with experience of the child welfare system, as well as the wider public. You will oversee the day-to-day management of our social media channels (Instagram, Facebook, BlueSky and LinkedIn), developing our digital presence, engaging with our target audiences, and increasing the charity’s reach. Communications at Family Rights Group is a team effort. You will work closely with colleagues across Family Rights Group, and particularly with our Content Creator and Digital Marketing Strategist in our Public Affairs and Communications team. You will collaborate on a dynamic, diverse content plan that amplifies our mission, with a focus on the voices and experiences of families and young people. This is a hands-on role that requires a strong interest in the child welfare system and our mission, combined with the technical expertise to be able to develop written and audio-visual content. Closing Date : 4 September 2026 Interview/Start Dates The closing time for applications is 9am. Shortlisted applicants will be invited to an online interview the following week. The starting date is as soon as possible after appointment, depending on the appointee's notice period. Application Details To apply, please go to the following page on our website: https://frg.org.uk/about-us/work-for-us/digital-communications-officer/ You will find more details including the full JD of the role, and application form to complete. Website : http://frg.org.uk

item.title: Parliamentary Caseworkers - Interim and Short-Term Assignments
item.description: Hive Support is a Community Interest Company providing specialist HR, recruitment and operational support to Members of Parliament and their offices. As a not-for-profit, we exist to strengthen the way parliamentary offices are staffed and run, and we work with MPs across Westminster and the constituencies to do that. We regularly provide experienced, short-term staffing support to MPs' offices, and demand for interim cover is growing. We are expanding our pool of experienced parliamentary professionals available for short-term assignments. We are particularly keen at present to hear from experienced caseworkers , though we welcome registrations across all parliamentary roles These opportunities typically arise to cover: Sickness absence Annual leave Short-term increases in workload Interim support during recruitment processes Assignments can vary in length, from a few weeks to several months, and may be offered on a full-time, part-time or flexible basis. Most roles can be undertaken remotely, while others may require a Westminster or constituency presence. Who we're looking for We are keen to hear from individuals who: Have prior experience working in a parliamentary office Can step into a role quickly and operate effectively with limited onboarding Are confident managing competing priorities in a fast-paced environment Have strong drafting and communication skills Experience may include: Casework IPSA and payroll processes Communications and press Research and policy Office management or Chief of Staff responsibilities Constituency support Secondments and additional work If you are currently employed by an MP, please note that your MP will need to approve any additional work under your IPSA contract. We encourage you to be clear on any contractual or procedural requirements in advance. We recognise that many candidates bring valuable transferable skills that are highly relevant to parliamentary roles, and we would be pleased to consider such applications for other opportunities we advertise. You will collaborate closely with the Director, marketing, product and operations teams to ensure commercial success. To include: • Developing and managing relationships with trainers and clients. • Agreeing and negotiating trainer fees, within fixed budgets. • Liaising with trainers to create course copy and materials. Chasing biographies, course materials, and presentations. • To build course websites and email templates. • Sending and coordinating pre-event questionnaires. • Ensuring courses are CPD certified. • Sending joining instructions to delegates, delivering customer and technical support, by phone, email or online. • Post-course follow up – to distribute evaluation forms and analyse results. To record costs and process trainer invoices. • To set up webinars on Zoom and arrange tech checks. • Client liaison for inhouse training. Personal Attributes and Experience: • Six months work experience in a professional setting. • Evidence of previous events/training experience. • Educated to degree level, minimum 2:1 or similar • Excellent IT skills e.g. Microsoft Office, Zoom. • Previous use of a virtual event platform (desirable), basic graphic design skills (desirable), email marketing or website building (desirable). • Excellent planning and organisational skills, accurate and meticulous. • Excellent customer service skills, enthusiastic and helpful approach. • Negotiation and commercial skills. • Reliable, good problem-solving skills. • A team player. • A good communicator, able to build relationships. item.title: Political Advisor
item.description: Hours: 37 Hours Per Week About the Role Are you interested in working in a political environment within a Local Unitary Authority? If so, then this could be the job for you! We are looking for an engaging, experienced and committed individual to join us as a Political Advisor for the Reform Group. This is an exciting and unique opportunity to provide a variety of services to the Reform Group, ranging from policy research and development to supporting senior Reform councillors in their strategic aims. You will be involved in note taking, organising meetings as well as assisting with wider duties required of you. You will provide high-quality political advice, policy research, and strategic support to the Reform Group Leader and Members of the Group, enabling effective decision‑making, policy development, and representation within the Council and across wider political and stakeholder networks. Sitting within the Governance Teams at the Council, you will act as a key link between the political group, council officers, and external partners, ensuring clear communication, alignment of priorities, and effective collaboration, including engagement with national and sector‑wide political structures. What We Are Looking For We are looking for someone who has: Experience and knowledge of providing high quality support to a team and working with others to complete projects to a high standard and on time. You will be highly organised with great ICT, English language and time management skills. You’ll be an effective communicator across the organisation, from residents and officers to senior managers and politicians. Experience of working in a political environment is desirable, as is a sound understanding of local government and its governance. Full support in all aspects of the role will be provided. Your work time will largely be based at the Civic Offices in Grays, Essex, with some opportunity to work from home. You may be expected to attend some evening events across the year. item.description: Location: Hybrid – minimum 2 days per week from London office and 2 days per month from the BVRLA office, River Lodge, Amersham, Bucks, HP7 0DD. Some UK travel and occasional overnight stays required. About the role The BVRLA is looking for a Campaigns Officer to support its award-nominated public affairs and campaign work. Working with our Public Affairs Manager in the Policy and Research team, you will support policy engagement campaigns, member mobilisation, political relationships and raising the profile of our work. You will join a talented, highly motivated and supportive team and work across fast-moving policy areas including electric vehicles, decarbonisation, future mobility, consumer finance and motor taxation. Key Tasks and Responsibilities Engage with MPs and staff, Select Committees and industry stakeholders to raise awareness of BVRLA, its members and policy priorities. Coordinate campaigns, strategies and programmes supporting BVRLA’s policy aims. Represent BVRLA at external working groups, conferences and third-party events. Support members to engage with MPs through the ‘Industry Champions’ programme. Lead BVRLA’s technical understanding of Bills passing through the Commons and Lords. Provide high-quality policy briefings for colleagues, MPs and members. Work with communications, compliance, training and events teams to maximise impact with Government, media and stakeholders. Distil BVRLA political and operational insight into accessible content for members. Provide content and administrative support for research projects, meetings and events. Professional and personal requirements Strong written and verbal communication skills. Solid understanding of UK Parliament, politics, procedure and policymaking. Self-starter with initiative, drive and creativity, able to multitask and engage potential new members. At least 1 year’s experience in a political environment, ideally in consultancy, think tank, media, trade association or Parliament. Excellent research skills, with the ability to distil complex topics into clear, accessible content for different audiences. Grit, determination and willingness to stretch themselves, learn and develop. Confident in media and social media relations, with the ability to support media coverage and reputation management. item.title: Senior Policy Officer
item.description: The NHS Alliance’s policy and analysis team shapes national policy and influences decision makers using evidence, expertise, and a deep understanding of our members’ experiences and aspirations for the NHS. We connect members and policymakers, provide clear and credible insight, and offer practical, workable solutions that respond to frontline realities. Through this, we strengthen our members’ collective voice and help ensure they can deliver the best possible care. We are looking for a senior policy officer to support the delivery of policy projects and contribute to the achievement of The NHS Alliance’s policy objectives. You will help to analyse policy developments and deliver projects to influence and translate government policy on behalf of members. As a senior policy officer, you will: Support the delivery of member-informed influencing activity and respond quickly to emerging issues. Observe, analyse and describe policy developments and their implications for members and the NHS. Work collaboratively with colleagues in other directorates and reflect wider NHS Alliance policy positions in content and activity. Draft policy content, such as reports, notes and briefings, and present work at internal meetings. Support delivery and scoping of funded projects, working with the commercial team when needed and provide administrative support where required. Support stakeholder and member engagement by preparing briefings, taking notes and sharing intelligence internally. Develop relationships with members and be comfortable working with senior NHS leaders. item.title: Research Manager
item.description: Join Us and Help Shape Brighter Futures At Depaul UK, we believe in people’s potential — and we take action every day to help unlock it. Whether you’re supporting young people directly or strengthening our organisation behind the scenes, your work will create real, lasting impact. Research Manager Ready to use research to drive real social change? Join us and lead high-impact research that influences policy, strengthens services, and amplifies the voices of people experiencing homelessness. You'll design and deliver robust mixed-methods research, turning data and lived experience into compelling evidence that shapes decisions and creates lasting impact. You will be an experienced researcher with strong qualitative and quantitative research skills, excellent analytical and writing ability, and a track record of delivering high-quality projects from concept to publication. You'll be confident managing multiple priorities, building relationships with stakeholders, and transforming complex findings into clear, meaningful insights. By joining our values-led organisation that is committed to ending homelessness, you'll have the opportunity to influence change at a national level, work flexibly as part of a collaborative team, and contribute to research that makes a tangible difference to people's lives. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds and experiences. Please note that this job opportunity is offered as a full-time (37.5 hours per week), permanent basis. In addition, this job offers a Hybrid working arrangement (in the office two days per week) working from one of our regions (London, Manchester or the North East); therefore, we welcome applications from different parts of the country. You will need to be able to travel throughout the UK and on occasions work out of hours. item.title: Parliamentary Assistant
item.description: The Rt Hon Graham Stuart MP is looking to recruit an organised, politically aware and highly motivated Parliamentary Assistant to join his team. This is an excellent opportunity to support the parliamentary work of an active constituency MP. The successful candidate will undertake research, prepare detailed briefings and help ensure Graham is fully informed on parliamentary, policy and constituency matters. The successful candidate will have excellent research and written communication skills, strong organisational skills, with experience of diary management and the ability to manage a varied workload in a fast-paced environment. Key Responsibilities Manage Graham's diary and ensure all entries are accurate and complete. Analyse, evaluate and interpret data to ensure Graham is accurately informed on key issues Assist in writing external communications including speeches. Compilation of briefing packs, take notes of meetings and draft appropriate submissions Develop and maintain current knowledge on relevant areas of parliamentary business and the local constituency. Engage confidentially, professionally, with care and integrity with members of the public, through telephone enquiries, social media, email and face to face Have working knowledge of relevant legislation and upcoming business including how they impact on the constituency Maintain positive on-going relationships with all parties including members of the public, groups, suppliers and Westminster where required Prepare and present briefing notes for committees, press releases, parliamentary questions etc. Respond to routine correspondence, including campaign emails and casework. To advise and ensure Graham is fully briefed on potential questions and motions to be put to the House Arrange parliamentary events. item.title: Caseworker/Senior Caseworker
item.description: Deirdre Costigan MP is seeking a Caseworker/Senior Caseworker to join her team, based in the Constituency Office in Southall with occasional work in Parliament. The successful candidate will support the team in managing constituency casework and contributing to wider policy and campaign work. The role includes liaising with government departments, local authorities and other organisations, drafting mass policy correspondence and identifying trends in casework to help inform parliamentary priorities. Key responsibilities Assist with arranging and attending MP advice surgeries, coffee mornings, community events and follow up as appropriate. Handle a high volume of routine enquiries and assist with more complex casework from members of the public via telephone, email and face-to-face interactions. Support Senior Caseworkers in progressing constituency casework and resolving constituent issues effectively. Research and draft mass campaign responses to constituents regarding government policy. Produce high-quality written responses to constituent enquiries. Identify trends and recurring issues arising from constituency casework and communicate these effectively to the Parliamentary team to help shape campaigns, policy priorities and parliamentary interventions. Ensure records are accurately maintained and information is managed confidentially in accordance with relevant data protection legislation. Ensure all cases are handled promptly, sensitively, confidentially and accurately, in accordance with the wishes and direction of the MP. Log all cases, monitor progress and ensure all identified actions are completed. Occasionally work outside normal office hours, including attending events with the MP when required. Essential Criteria Excellent written communication skills and the ability to draft letters and emails to a high professional standard. A proactive approach to work, both independently and as part of a small team. Ability to work in a fast-paced environment and manage competing priorities. Commitment to the aims and values of the Labour Party. Desirable Criteria Previous casework experience. Experience of using casework management software. Ealing Southall is a very diverse constituency and knowledge of a relevant community language, e.g. Punjabi would be desirable. Upon appointment you will be required to comply with the Baseline Personnel Security Standard, undertaken by the Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO). See Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO) page for further info. MPs generally pay staff in accordance with IPSA guidelines . item.title: Senior Caseworker
item.description: Chris Murray is looking to recruit an experienced caseworker to join his team in Edinburgh and manage the office’s casework output and processes. The Senior Caseworker will support Chris to be an active, impactful and approachable MP. You will lead the casework function and work with a Caseworker to provide advice and support to local people on a range of issues. Managing a large caseload, organising MP surgeries, and supporting relevant events, you will help resolve problems for local people through communication with government agencies, local authorities, the voluntary sector and other organisations. The successful candidate will be a proven problem solver with a high level of written and verbal communication. Existing experience within a casework environment would be an advantage and what is essential is the ability to deal with high volumes of correspondence combined with a genuine concern for the lives of the constituents. The key responsibilities are as follows: • Assist with surgeries and other meetings and follow up as appropriate • Ensure all cases are logged; monitor progress and ensure all identified actions are taken • Ensure records are kept and information managed confidentially and in line with data protection legislation • Exercise a level of autonomy in reaching decisions on cases based on the evidence • Gather relevant information to resolve or progress cases • Liaise with Government agencies, voluntary sector and others to resolve constituency matters • Manage a large caseload of complex cases, working in a professional, confidential, caring and sensitive manner • Respond professionally, sensitively, confidentially and with integrity to routine correspondence and enquiries by email, telephone, social media and face to face from constituents, the media, lobbyists and pressure groups Required skills and values: • Ability to deal with and prioritise a large and varied caseload, and work well under pressure • Ability to manage expectations in sometimes challenging circumstances • Excellent interpersonal and written communication skills • Ability to work independently as well as effectively as part of a small team • Ability and willingness to work outside of normal hours and travel for work occasionally • Sympathetic to the aims, values and objectives of the Labour Party Upon appointment you will be required to comply with the Baseline Personnel Security Standard, undertaken by the Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO). item.description: Miatta Fahnbulleh MP is looking for a dynamic and highly committed individual for the role of Caseworker in her busy Peckham Constituency office. Key Responsibilities will include: Assist with surgeries and other constituency meetings and follow up as appropriate. Deal with large numbers of standard queries, as well as assisting with more complex cases from members of the public by phone, email, social media or face to face. Ongoing communication may be required. Draft responses to constituents. Ensure that each case is dealt with promptly, sensitively, confidentially and accurately in accordance with the MP. Self-motivated with the ability to work independently, while also working effectively as part of a small team alongside the Senior Caseworker. Support the aims and values of The Labour Party. item.title: Parliamentary Researcher
item.description: About the role I was elected in May 2026 to represent the Highlands and Islands, Scotland's largest parliamentary region. The people here face a distinct set of challenges: depopulation, a shortage of housing, centralised healthcare, inadequate infrastructure, and renewable energy projects reshaping rural and coastal communities — alongside the enduring concerns of fishing and farming. I'm looking for a bright, driven Parliamentary Researcher to join my team and help me stand up for them. It's a rare chance to get involved at an early stage across all of my work, in Parliament and across the Region, with real scope to grow and progress over the five-year term. What you'll do You'll start by supporting me across three areas, and take on more as you find your feet: Research: Dig into the policy, legislation and issues that matter to the Highlands and Islands, and get to grips with the facts and figures behind them Turn that into clear, accurate briefings and speaking notes for the chamber and beyond Communications: Draft press releases, articles and social media posts, and help run my Facebook and Instagram Help with local campaigns and day-to-day media enquiries Parliament: Draft parliamentary questions, motions and debate contributions Support the smooth running of my office and, as Reform's Parliamentary Business Manager, the group's business and Whips Office. About you Having done this job myself at Holyrood, I know that raw talent, drive and a genuine desire to learn count for far more than a polished CV. I'd happily take on someone with real ability and train them up. I expect parts of this role to be new to whomever I appoint, what matters is the ability to pick things up fast. You might be an ambitious graduate or early-career professional looking to work at the heart of Scottish politics. What I'm looking for: A sharp mind and the ability to learn quickly Strong writing, and a feel for turning detail into a clear argument Drive, initiative and sound judgement A real interest in politics, current affairs and the Highlands and Islands Desirable, but not essential: A strong connection to, or knowledge of, the local issues in the Highlands, Moray or the Islands Familiarity with video editing or graphics software (e.g. Adobe) — though a willingness to learn is enough Closing Date : 4 September 2026 Interview/Start Dates Interviews will be held in person at the Scottish Parliament. These will be done on a rolling basis, so early applications are encouraged. Application Details Please send a CV and a short covering letter explaining your interest in the role to max.bannerman.msp@parliament.scot Website : https://reformuk.scot/

item.title: Parliamentary Researcher
item.description: James Cartlidge, Conservative MP for South Suffolk and Shadow Secretary of State for Defence, is looking for a full-time Parliamentary Researcher to join his Westminster office. You will work in a small, busy team supporting the MP across his Shadow Cabinet responsibilities, with defence at the heart of the brief. This is a role for someone who can turn complex material into clear, usable writing at pace. You will be researching policy and legislation, drafting speeches, parliamentary questions and briefing packs, and keeping the MP ahead of developments in defence, foreign affairs and wider government policy. The pace is fast and the subject matter is high profile, so you will need to hold several deadlines at once without losing accuracy. A strong interest in or knowledge of defence, security and international affairs will serve you well. That said, we are just as interested in people who can research and write to a high standard from other policy backgrounds, so if that describes you, please apply. For full details please visit: https://recruitment.hivesupport.co.uk/job/35549/parliamentary-researcher-to-james-cartlidge-mp/london Closing Date : 31 August 2026 Interview/Start Dates Interviews: week commencing 7th September Start date: as soon as possible following pre-employment checks Application Details Apply online at: https://recruitment.hivesupport.co.uk/job/35549/parliamentary-researcher-to-james-cartlidge-mp/london Website : https://www.jamescartlidge.com/

item.title: Communications Officer
item.description: Sureena Brackenridge MP is looking for a highly motivated, politically aware and skilled communications professional to join her team as a Communications Officer. You will play an essential role in communicating Sureena’s work to constituents across Wolverhampton North East and supporting her as an active and visible MP. Based in the constituency office, you will work closely with the team to coordinate and deliver media, digital and campaign communications across Westminster and the constituency, demonstrating the impact of Sureena’s work. You will develop and deliver constituency campaigns, identifying opportunities to turn local issues and casework into campaigns, and producing communications that engage constituents and key stakeholders. You will monitor media and social media activity, identify opportunities, suggest creative content to grow reach and engagement, and analyse feedback and data to inform messaging and priorities. The role may be Part Time or Full Time, so please make clear your preference in the application. If you have experience in a communications or media environment, we would like to hear from you. The ideal candidate will have: • Excellent written and verbal communication skills • Strong experience in media, social media and/or digital communications • Strong digital content creation and delivery skills • Understanding of digital media trends and campaigning • Excellent research, analytical and problem-solving skills Key responsibilities: • Develop targeted communications and issue-based campaigns across a range of platforms • Monitor local, regional and national media and social media, identifying relevant issues, trends and opportunities • Create, edit and publish engaging digital and social media content • Identify opportunities to turn local issues and casework into campaigns • Draft external communications, press releases and public statements • Produce clear briefings, reports and follow-ups for meetings and events • Organise community surveys and analyse feedback to inform the Member’s work • Support stakeholder engagement and wider campaign activity • Maintain confidential records in line with the Data Protection Act • Undertake general office administration and work flexibly, including occasional evenings, weekends or travel Upon appointment you will be required to comply with the Baseline Personnel Security Standard, undertaken by the Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO). See Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO) page for further info. MPs generally pay staff in accordance with IPSA guidelines . item.title: Parliamentary Assistant
item.description: Samantha Niblett MP is looking for a Parliamentary Assistant to support her parliamentary and constituency work, with a particular focus on ensuring the voice of South Derbyshire and her constituents is represented in Parliament. The role will cover research, analysis, communications, parliamentary business, stakeholder engagement and general office support. Main responsibilities will include: • Researching parliamentary, national and local issues and assessing their impact on South Derbyshire. • Keeping up to date with parliamentary business, including legislation, Motions, debates and Hansard, and preparing briefings, speeches, parliamentary questions and other material for the MP. • Drafting articles, press releases and social media content, and monitoring media and social media for relevant issues and trends. • Attending meetings, taking notes and progressing actions. • Supporting diary management, correspondence, enquiries and general administration. • Building positive relationships with constituents, community groups, organisations and Westminster contacts. • Working with colleagues across communications and casework to ensure research and information are used effectively. • Maintaining accurate records and files in accordance with data protection requirements. Capabilities required: • Excellent communication, research, analytical and problem-solving skills. • Good political judgement and the ability to understand complex issues and their local impact. • Highly organised, adaptable and able to prioritise and work to tight deadlines. • A self-starter who can use initiative and work independently while contributing effectively to a small team. • Strong interpersonal skills, with the ability to engage professionally and sensitively with the public. • Discretion, integrity and the ability to handle confidential information. • Strong IT and administrative skills. Desirable experience: Experience in a political, parliamentary, communications, public affairs or research environment; knowledge of Parliament and its processes; an understanding of South Derbyshire; and experience producing briefings, speeches, press releases or digital content. There may be a requirement to work outside normal hours and travel occasionally for work. Upon appointment you will be required to comply with the Baseline Personnel Security Standard, undertaken by the Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO). item.title: Assistant Teaching Professor in Environmental and Political Geography (Part Time, Fixed Term)
item.description: The Department of Geography wishes to appoint a 0.6 FTE five-year fixed-term Assistant Teaching Professor in Environmental and Political Geography, starting from 1 October 2026. Within the 0.6 FTE pro rata limits, the main responsibilities of the role will be a focus on Outreach and Widening Participation, curriculum development and teaching leadership, and on contributing to Departmental policy on AI in and for teaching and assessment. As appropriate, the applicant will also plan, prepare and deliver lectures, seminars and practical classes for students on the Geography undergraduate degree and, where appropriate, Master's programmes, with a focus on environmental and political geographies, and research skills and methods. An interest in the Pacific and Small-Island States is desirable. They will also contribute to relevant examination and assessment of these courses. The successful candidate will hold a PhD in Environmental and/or Political Geography, or a cognate subject. They will possess evidence of extensive and relevant teaching experience in related fields. The successful candidate will demonstrate close familiarity with the relevant fields through high-quality research publications. Applicants should submit the following documents with their application: Full Curriculum Vitae (CV) A statement (two-three pages maximum) on the applicant's experiences and plans in relation to teaching and research (this should include evidence of teaching leadership, including curriculum development); outreach and widening participation; and on engagement with AI in HE pedagogy. The contact details of two referees. More information about the role is available on the Further Particulars document attached. Fixed-term: The funds for this post are available for 5 years in the first instance. To apply online for this vacancy and to view further information about the role, please click the 'Apply' button above. If you have any questions on the role and/or the application process, please email Mrs Alessandra Uomo, HR Coordinator, at hr@geog.cam.ac.uk . Interviews are anticipated to take place in Cambridge on Tuesday, 1st September 2026. Please quote reference LC50692 on your application and in any correspondence about this vacancy. item.title: Research Associate in the Politics of military labour association in Europe
item.description: We are looking to appoint a postdoctoral research associate with expertise in military power, military work and labour, the politics of unions, and/or critical and feminist approaches, to contribute to the delivery of a research project on the politics of military labour association and military unionisation in Europe. This is an excellent opportunity for a postdoctoral researcher to undertake research at the intersection of critical military studies, critical and feminist international relations and political economy, and to contribute to the development of scholarship on and knowledge exchange and impact relating to the politics of military labour. The role will involve reviewing and synthesising academic literature, data collection (conducting interviews and creating a corpus of texts from contemporary and archival sources), qualitative data analysis, knowledge exchange and impact activities, contributing to the organisation of events, and writing outputs for academic and non-academic audiences. We are seeking a candidate with a PhD (at or near completion) in politics, international relations, political economy or a cognate field and with expertise in relation to military power, military work and labour, the politics of unions, and/or critical and feminist approaches. Candidates should have experience producing high quality research and writing, the ability to write for different audiences, experience with qualitative social science methodologies, effective communication skills, the ability to contribute to event organisation, and the ability to work independently and closely with a team. Experience working with non-academic partners and stakeholders would be desirable. The project, funded by a standard grant from the Economic and Social Research Council (ESRC), will be based in the School of Sociological Studies, Politics and International Relations and led by Dr Joanna Tidy. The successful candidate will join a our large and collegial School and will become part of our internationally recognised research community. You will join one or more of our active and supportive research clusters (for instance, political economy or international politics) and there are opportunities for interdisciplinary engagement across the Faculty and University.

item.title: Research Fellow
item.description: Salary: Full time starting salary is normally in the range £36,636 to £46,049 with potential progression once in post to £48,822 Contract Type: Fixed Term Contract until Sept 2029 Work within the TRACE project and contribute to writing bids Operate within area of specialism of Gender-Based Violence Analyse and interpret research findings and results Publish scholarly outputs in conjunction with team members Contribute to generating funding The TRACE project is a Horizon Europe funded research programme examining technology-facilitated gender-based violence (TFGBV) across the conflict, transit and refuge continuum. The project brings together an international consortium of researchers and stakeholders to generate robust, comparative evidence and inform policy and practice. TRACE aims to build the first cross-context evidence base on TFGBV across diverse geographical and socio-political settings, to develop a shared typology and methodological framework to support consistent analysis and comparison, and to produce evidence-based guidance to strengthen policy, prevention strategies and accountability mechanisms. We are seeking a highly motivated Research Associate to join the Horizon Europe funded TRACE project, an international research programme examining technology-facilitated gender-based violence across the conflict, transit and refuge continuum. The successful candidate will contribute to cutting-edge, interdisciplinary research, working as part of a multi-partner consortium to generate comparative evidence, inform policy and practice, and support meaningful societal impact. Person spec A PhD relevant to the research area (or near completion), or equivalent PhD level qualifications. High level analytical capability Ability to communicate complex information clearly Fluency in relevant models, techniques or methods and ability to contribute to developing new ones Ability to assess resource requirements and use resources effectively Understanding of and ability to contribute to broader management/administration processes Contribute to the planning and organising of the research programme and/or specific research project Co-ordinate own work with others to avoid conflict or duplication of effort Experience of gender and trauma sensitive interviewing Proficiency in Arabic or another relevant language spoken by forced migrant communities, sufficient to conduct research interviews without an interpreter. Knowledge of the protected characteristics and duties under the Equality Act 2010. Including fostering good relations and advancing the universities Public Sector Equality Duty (PSED). Other relevant criteria from our equality and diversity knowledge, skills and experience document. Informal enquiries can be made to Professor Jenny Phillimore j.a.phillimore@bham.ac.uk To download the full job description and details of this position and submit an electronic application online please click on the ' Apply ' button above. Valuing excellence, sustaining investment We value diversity and inclusion at the University of Birmingham and welcome applications from all sections of the community and are open to discussions around all forms of flexible working

item.title: Hatton Professorship of Sustainability
item.description: The Board of Electors to the Hatton Professorship of Sustainability invite applications for this Professorship from persons whose work falls within the general field of the Professorship (combining behavioural sciences and sustainability studies) to take up appointment on 1 July 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. Candidates will have an outstanding research record of international stature in a relevant area of study (includes experimental psychology, social neuroscience, behavioural economics, consumer behaviour, political science, policy studies, and environmental social sciences, as well as allied disciplines). The ideal candidate will demonstrate a commitment to the applications of research to address real world sustainability problems, working in combination with governments, businesses and civil society partners to design and monitor the impacts of interventions. They will be solution orientated with a special focus on individual, corporate and collective action towards environmental sustainability. They will be expected to demonstrate the vision, leadership, experience and enthusiasm to build on current strengths in maintaining and developing a leading research presence. They will hold a PhD or equivalent postgraduate qualification. Standard professorial duties include teaching and research, examining, supervision and administration. The Professor will be based in Cambridge. A competitive salary will be offered. To apply online for this vacancy and to view further information about the role, please click 'Apply' above. Further information is available at: http://www.hr.admin.cam.ac.uk or contact the Human Resources, University Offices, The Old Schools, Cambridge, CB2 1TT, (email: professorships@admin.cam.ac.uk ). Applications, consisting of a letter of application, a statement of current and future research plans, a curriculum vitae and a publications list, along with details of three referees should be made online no later than 5 October 2026. Informal enquiries may be directed to Professor Bhaskar Vira (Convenor of Board of Electors): ProVCEducation@admin.cam.ac.uk Please quote reference LA50727 on your application and in any correspondence about this vacancy. The University actively supports equality, diversity and inclusion and encourages applications from all sections of society. item.title: Assistant Professor in Comparative Politics
item.description: The School of Government and International Affairs (SGIA) at Durham University seeks to appoint an exceptional scholar as an Assistant Professor with research and teaching expertise in Comparative Politics, whose work uses quantitative research methods and has a regional focus on Africa, Asia, Latin America or the Middle East. This post offers an exciting opportunity to make a major contribution to the development of internationally excellent research and teaching while allowing unrivalled opportunities to progress and embed your career in an exciting and progressive institution. For more information, please visit our School page at School of Government and International Affairs - Durham University as well as the web page of the Centre for Institutions and Political Behaviour - Durham University The successful candidate will benefit from individual research support funding, access to SGIA and University-wide research funding and be entitled to apply for sabbatical leave on a basis of one term of leave in each seven terms of service. SGIA and Durham University provides high-quality administrative support to assist with applications for research funding, to facilitate research-based engagement and impact work with non-academic communities, and to enable the introduction and dissemination of new educational practice. The successful candidate will get involved in the development of our research community in Comparative Politics, including its connections with other Durham departments and other institutions, and innovative educational practice to enhance the learning experience of both undergraduate and postgraduate students, including PhD candidates. Among other EDI initiatives, the department is currently in the process of diversifying its curriculum, and this is a project we would be keen on the post-holder to contribute to. For more information, please visit our department pages at www.dur.ac.uk/sgia/
